title: New skill: revalidate-done-tasks — periodic audit that done tasks are still actually done
description: A task's `state: "done"` records a snapshot of what was true when `pr-reviewer`/`pr-decision` last checked it — nothing currently re-checks that claim later. `orchestrate-tasks` only ever moves the board forward, so a later change elsewhere in the codebase (a deleted file, a renamed function, a quietly-removed test) could silently invalidate an earlier 'done' task's checklist claims without anything catching it. Create a new `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks` skill that iterates every task under `docs/tasks/done/`, re-verifies each checklist item still holds against the current repository state (referenced files/functions still exist and do what the checklist claims), confirms the project's full test suites + coverage gates still pass overall (one full run is enough evidence for all done tasks, not a per-task re-run), and reports any task whose done-claim no longer holds — without silently fixing anything itself, matching the project's existing read-only-audit-agent pattern (e.g. `architecture-reviewer`, `elder-signal-reviewer`).

checklist.step: Design the audit's scope/mechanism — e.g. dispatching `task-qa-reviewer` once per done task vs. a single lighter-weight direct pass — and record the choice with rationale as a `decisions` entry, weighing thoroughness against the cost of potentially dispatching dozens of subagents on every run.
Create `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md` implementing the chosen approach, following existing skill file conventions.

Decide what the skill does with a task it finds no longer holds — most consistent with the project's existing rules is to flag it (revert `state` away from `done`, record a `decisions`/`questions` entry explaining why) rather than attempt an autonomous fix, matching the pipeline's existing philosophy of tracking findings on the board rather than an audit silently rewriting code — record as a `decisions` entry.
Register the new skill in CLAUDE.md's Skills list.
Run it once for real against the current (fully-done) board as a smoke test and report what it found (ideally nothing, confirming the board is currently accurate) before considering this done.
